visualReview.notes: Inspected the museum campus from four directions and the detailed views of the Shrine, square pool and basalt wall, terraced stone gallery modules, dark clerestories and the screened north pavilions. The Shrine’s white shell shows its flared shoulders, narrow neck and open crown.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected the ten shared-material views. The limestone, concrete, dark glazing, white ceramic and basalt surfaces resolve in the close frames. The flat fixture hides only the low bases of some hillside geometry. The independently inspected terrain shows their grade relationship.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected 26 current frames and all four detail-level transitions. All four keep the crescent of gallery masses, separate arrival buildings and the Shrine with its companion wall and pool. Distant galleries group into larger modules. Near views add bay mullions and individually defined horizontal louvers.

geographicReview.notes: The mapped 45-corner collection block, northern pavilion, three named or measured gallery parts and Shrine roof are retained. The independently captured 512 m terrain shows the staggered museum campus on the original hillside. Gallery floor levels, retaining edges and above-grade basalt wall exposure are estimates.

fidelityReview.scope: The present Israel Museum campus exterior in Jerusalem, including the original terraced gallery pavilions, 2010 visitor circulation pavilions, named northern pavilion and Shrine of the Book with its pool and basalt wall.
fidelityReview.notes: First-party design accounts establish the repeated limestone modules, cantilevered clerestory roofs, contemporary glass screens and circulation sequence. The direct CC0 original and Kiesler’s account establish the Shrine profile, stone pool, black basalt contrast and oculus. Roof elevations beyond the three mapped parts, the exact gallery arrangements and the basalt wall registration are estimated. Artworks and interiors are outside the exterior scope.

imageryReview.notes: The cleared Qualla media were checked first. Those public-domain and CC0 items show exhibits. The independently verified exact public-domain dedication from photographer Gary Todd supplies one exterior angle of the Shrine. Its bytes match the Commons transfer. The galleries use original terrain, mapped geometry and written design descriptions.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: Israel Museum’s standing collection pavilions, north public entry, and Shrine of the Book complex in Jerusalem.

limitations: The native contours and three mapped pavilion heights fix the campus layout. Gallery-by-gallery roof schedules, sections, surface transitions and smaller terraces are estimated from the recorded modular design.
The model includes the standing gallery and visitor buildings and the Shrine of the Book above ground. The Jerusalem maquette, artworks, interiors and museum annexes are outside the scope.

The Shrine’s exterior profile uses the photographer’s verified CC0 original. The wall dimensions recorded by Kiesler include the portion beside the sunken court. Its above-terrace height, wall orientation and any local terrain contact are estimates.
